title: Simultaneous affine shrinking below finitely many finite maps
statement: Let V be a scheme, η a point, and t_i:T_i→V finitely many finite morphisms. Suppose open O_i⊆T_i contains every point over η. Then an affine open U⊆V containing η has t_i⁻¹(U)⊆O_i for every i. This includes an empty family and does not require Noetherian hypotheses. [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]

proof.text: Each finite morphism is closed, so t_i(T_i minus O_i) is closed and avoids η. The union of these finitely many images is closed and avoids η. Choose an affine neighbourhood of η inside its complement. Any point in an inverse image outside O_i would put its image in this union. The empty union imposes no condition.

theorem exists_affine_neighbourhood_below_finite_maps
    (V : Scheme.{u}) (η : V) (n : ℕ) (T : Fin n → Scheme.{u})
    (t : ∀ i, T i ⟶ V) [∀ i, IsFinite (t i)] (O : ∀ i, (T i).Opens)
    (hO : ∀ i (x : T i), t i x = η → x ∈ O i) :
    ∃ (U : V.Opens), η ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∀ i, (t i) ⁻¹ᵁ U ≤ O i
